runs.question: What does the memo require agencies to do within 180 days? I mean OMB M-25-21, the April 2025 memo.

answer.text:
The 180-day requirement in M-25-21 is a compliance-plan filing. Its clock starts at the memo's issuance or at any later update. Consistent with Section 104( c) and ( d) of the AI in Government Act of 2020, within 180 days of the issuance of this memorandum or any update to this memorandum, and every two years thereafter until 2036, each agency must submit to 0MB and post publicly on the agency's website either a plan to achieve consistency with this memorandum, or a written determination that the agency does not use and does not anticipate using covered AL

The filing can take one of two forms: a plan for aligning with the memo, or a written statement that the agency neither uses nor expects to use covered AI. Any plan also has to address existing internal AI rules. Those rules need revising so they match the memo's requirements. OMB will provide templates for these compliance plans.

Note that the same passage makes the filing recurring, not a one-time task. It repeats every two years until 2036.

Two caveats:
- **A different deadline applies to policy updates.** The 270-day deadline covers a separate task. Within 270 days of the issuance of this memorandum, agencies must revisit and update where necessary their internal policies on IT infrastructure, and the same passage covers data, cybersecurity, and privacy policies.
- **M-24-10 is no longer the governing text.** The 2025 memo states that this memorandum rescinds and replaces Office of Management and Budget (0MB) Memorandum M-24-10, Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use ofArtificial Intelligence. The earlier answer quoted M-24-10's compliance-plan language as if it were current, so disregard that for present purposes.

data.text:
The 180-day requirement in M-25-21 is a compliance-plan filing. Its clock starts at the memo's issuance or at any later update. Consistent with Section 104( c) and ( d) of the AI in Government Act of 2020, within 180 days of the issuance of this memorandum or any update to this memorandum, and every two years thereafter until 2036, each agency must submit to 0MB and post publicly on the agency's website either a plan to achieve consistency with this memorandum, or a written determination that the agency does not use and does not anticipate using covered AL

The filing can take one of two forms: a plan for aligning with the memo, or a written statement that the agency neither uses nor expects to use covered AI. Any plan also has to address existing internal AI rules. Those rules need revising so they match the memo's requirements. OMB will provide templates for these compliance plans.

Note that the same passage makes the filing recurring, not a one-time task. It repeats every two years until 2036.

Two caveats:
- **A different deadline applies to policy updates.** The 270-day deadline covers a separate task. Within 270 days of the issuance of this memorandum, agencies must revisit and update where necessary their internal policies on IT infrastructure, and the same passage covers data, cybersecurity, and privacy policies.
- **M-24-10 is no longer the governing text.** The 2025 memo states that this memorandum rescinds and replaces Office of Management and Budget (0MB) Memorandum M-24-10, Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use ofArtificial Intelligence. The earlier answer quoted M-24-10's compliance-plan language as if it were current, so disregard that for present purposes.
